title: Soft Coconut Milk Coco Bread
summary: Pillowy, pale half-moon buns made with warm coconut milk and butter, folded so they split open neatly around a patty or just a spread of butter.
equipment: large bowl or stand mixer with dough hook
2 baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Stir the flour, yeast, sugar and salt together in a large bowl. Mix the coconut milk, warmed to about 38 °C, with the 50 g melted butter, pour it in and bring everything into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Warm liquid gets the yeast going quickly, and the coconut fat keeps the crumb tender.

steps.title: Knead until smooth
steps.text: Knead for 8-10 minutes by hand, or 5-6 minutes in a mixer with the dough hook, until the dough is smooth, elastic and springs back when pressed. A well-developed dough holds the gas that makes these buns so light.

steps.title: First rise
steps.text: Cover and leave somewhere warm for 1-1½ hours, until doubled in size and puffy. A finger pressed gently into the top should leave a dent that fills back slowly.

steps.title: Divide and rest
steps.text: Tip the dough onto a lightly floured surface and divide it into 8 pieces of about 115 g. Roll each into a smooth ball, cover and rest for 10 minutes. The short rest relaxes the gluten so the balls roll out without shrinking back.

steps.title: Roll, butter and fold
steps.text: Grease the trays with the 10 g butter. Roll each ball into a round about 15 cm across and 4 mm thick, brush the top lightly with melted butter and fold it in half into a half-moon, pressing the curved edge gently. The butter layer stops the two halves fusing, so each bun opens cleanly once baked.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Set the buns well apart on the trays, cover loosely and leave for 30-45 minutes until puffy. Spacing them gives each bun room to rise without merging into its neighbour.

steps.title: Bake gently
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175 °C (155 °C fan) and bake for 18-22 minutes, until just set and only very lightly golden underneath. The tops should stay pale and matt rather than brown or shiny, and the centre should read 88-93 °C. A moderate oven cooks the enriched dough through before the sugar and fat on the surface can colour.

steps.title: Brush and steam
steps.text: Brush the hot buns lightly with the remaining melted butter, then stack them in a folded tea towel while any others bake. Trapped steam softens the crust, giving the characteristic tender, fluffy finish.

tips: Check the coconut milk temperature: much above 40 °C can slow or harm the yeast, so aim for comfortably warm, not hot.
A common mistake is over-baking until the tops turn golden; coco bread should stay pale, so start checking the temperature at 18 minutes.
Brush only a light film of butter before folding; too much makes the halves slide apart as they prove.
Split and fill while warm, or reheat briefly wrapped in foil to bring back the softness.
storage: Keep cooled buns in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Warm wrapped in foil in a low oven for a few minutes before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
